*   **When Not to Use:** When the volume is small and polygonal rendering is sufficient. [S3, book] When hardware does not support required features (volumetric textures, render-to-texture) [S1].

The claim states that ray-casting is suitable 'When the volume is small'. However, Source [S3] explicitly argues that ray-tracing becomes competitive with hardware z-buffers (polygonal rendering) only for 'sufficiently large datasets' (e.g., greater than several million polygons) because its low time complexity overcomes its large time constant. It suggests that for small datasets, the large time constant makes ray-tracing slower than polygonal rendering. Therefore, the evidence contradicts the claim that ray-casting is the preferred method when the volume is small.

This method is a real-time rendering pipeline for implicit surfaces defined by a regular volumetric grid of samples, using ray-casting on graphics hardware to directly render the isosurface without intermediate polygonal representation [S1][S3, book].

The claim states that the method is a real-time rendering pipeline for implicit surfaces defined by a regular volumetric grid, using ray-casting on graphics hardware to directly render the isosurface without intermediate polygonal representation. Source [S1] explicitly describes a 'real-time rendering pipeline for implicit surfaces defined by a regular volumetric grid of samples' that 'uses ray-casting on graphics hardware to perform a direct rendering of the isosurface' and notes that shading operations are deferred to image space (implying no intermediate polygonal mesh is generated for rendering). Source [S3] corroborates this by describing an 'interactive isosurface rendering technique' that 'generates images directly via ray-tracing without intermediate polygonal representation' for 'very large datasets' (implying real-time/interactive capability). Both sources confirm the core components: real-time/interactive, implicit surfaces, regular volumetric grid, ray-casting/tracing on hardware, and direct rendering without polygons.
